methodological_rigor.justification: The design is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, 1:1 randomized phase 3 trial (RATIONALE-309) with stratified randomization by sex and liver metastatic status, IRC-assessed PFS as the pre-specified primary endpoint per protocol, and the ITT population used for efficacy — all appropriate for the question. Statistical methods are standard and well-chosen: Kaplan-Meier with Brookmeyer-Crowley CIs, stratified Cox models for HRs, and two crossover-adjusted sensitivity analyses (RPSFTM and 2-stage with bootstrapped CIs) to address the 52.3% crossover rate in the placebo arm. Weaknesses include the exploratory nature of the biomarker analyses without multiplicity correction across many subgroup HRs (hot/cold TME, B-cell, T-cell, DC signatures, PD-L1 cutoffs), limited power for OS at this follow-up (OS HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.51–1.05 crosses 1), and the acknowledged assumption of no unmeasured confounders in the 2-stage model with only 37 control-arm participants. No new power calculation is reported for this 3-year follow-up analysis; limitations are explicitly discussed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a secondary long-term follow-up analysis of an individual phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled RCT, mapping to Oxford LoE 1b. Clinical relevance is high: NPC in the recurrent/metastatic setting has an unmet need, endpoints include OS (patient-relevant) and PFS, and the regimen is already approved by the European Commission and Chinese NMPA — this long-term update directly informs practice. The B-cell signature biomarker finding (HR 0.41; 95% CI 0.23–0.74 for OS) offers a plausible path toward predictive biomarker development beyond PD-L1 TC expression, though it remains exploratory and needs prospective validation.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript explicitly follows the CONSORT reporting guideline, provides a patient disposition figure (Figure 1), registers the trial (NCT03924986), references the full protocol and SAP in supplements, and reports pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints with detailed AE grading per CTCAE v5.0 and immune-mediated AE definitions. Patient flow, randomization method (interactive response technology, stratified), blinding, inclusion criteria, treatment regimens, and discontinuations are well described. Data availability is weak as presented: no mention of a public data repository, no code sharing statement, and biomarker platform details (HTG EdgeSeq, NextSeq 500, ConsensusClusterPlus) rely on a prior publication for methodological detail. Industry-trial data-sharing posture is typical but limits reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: The core efficacy finding is a long-term confirmation and extension of the previously published RATIONALE-309 interim analysis (ref 14, Cancer Cell 2023) and sits alongside JUPITER-02 and CAPTAIN-1st trials demonstrating similar PD-1 + chemo benefit in R/M NPC — thus the primary efficacy update is incremental confirmation. The meaningful novel contribution is the exploratory biomarker analysis correlating B-cell gene expression signatures (and hot/cold TME) with OS benefit from anti–PD-1 therapy in NPC, extending prior PFS-focused observations and chemo-only B-cell survival data (Lv et al.). This is a reasonable but still incremental empirical and methodological extension; the predictive biomarker claim awaits prospective validation and does not displace PD-L1 or reframe the field.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written, logically organized, and uses the JAMA structured abstract format. Methods are concise but reference supplements for depth, results are presented in a conventional endpoint-by-endpoint order, and the discussion engages comparator trials (JUPITER-02, CAPTAIN-1st) and prior biomarker literature well. The abstract contains some structural redundancy typical of the JAMA question/finding/meaning format but remains quantitatively accurate and self-contained. Figure captions for the PFS and OS curves provide event counts, medians, 95% CIs, and landmark survival rates, enabling standalone interpretation.

key_strengths: Phase 3 double-blind placebo-controlled RCT with stratified randomization and IRC-assessed primary PFS endpoint
Mature 3-year OS data with two pre-specified crossover-adjustment methods (RPSFTM, 2-stage) addressing 52.3% crossover
Explicit CONSORT adherence, protocol/SAP in supplements, and NCT03924986 registration
Clinically meaningful OS improvement (45.3 vs 31.8 months) in a disease area with real unmet need; already supports regulatory approvals
Exploratory B-cell gene signature biomarker (OS HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.23–0.74) offers a predictive-marker hypothesis beyond PD-L1
key_concerns: Primary PFS/OS findings are a long-term update of an already-published interim analysis — novelty is incremental
ITT OS HR 95% CI (0.51–1.05) crosses 1; sustained OS benefit depends on crossover-adjusted supportive analyses with their own assumptions
Biomarker subgroup analyses are exploratory with no multiplicity correction across many signatures and cutoffs
No public data/code repository stated; reproducibility of GEP pipeline relies on reference to prior publication
Asian-only population limits generalizability to keratinizing NPC settings (acknowledged)
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically solid, well-reported long-term update of a registration-grade phase 3 trial with a credible exploratory predictive biomarker signal; the incremental nature versus the published interim analysis and the exploratory biomarker caveats place it at the top of Tier 3 to lower Tier 2, with Tier 2 achievable after minor clarifications on multiplicity and data availability.
